question: Can a pure ConvNet, modernized with design and training choices borrowed from vision Transformers, match hierarchical Transformers such as Swin on accuracy, scalability and downstream tasks?
hypothesis: Much of the Transformer advantage in vision comes from training recipe and macro/micro design choices, not self-attention itself, so a ConvNet that adopts them should close the gap.
contributions: A step-by-step roadmap modernizing ResNet toward Swin-T/B without attention
ConvNeXt family (T/S/B/L/XL) competitive with Swin on ImageNet, COCO and ADE20K
Evidence that the ConvNet inductive bias keeps efficiency and scalability

method.summary: Start from ResNet-50/200 trained with a DeiT/Swin-style recipe, then apply stepwise changes (stage ratio, patchify stem, depthwise conv with wider channels, inverted bottleneck, 7x7 kernels, GELU, fewer activations and norms, LN, separate downsampling) and track ImageNet-1K top-1. The resulting ConvNeXt family is scaled with ImageNet-22K pretraining and evaluated on ImageNet-1K, COCO and ADE20K.
method.task: image classification, object detection/instance segmentation, semantic segmentation

training.lr_schedule: cosine decay after linear warmup; finetune cosine with layer-wise lr decay 0.7 (B/L from IN-1K) or 0.8 (IN-22K), no warmup
training.warmup: 20 epochs linear (IN-1K); 5 epochs (IN-22K); 50 epochs for isotropic
training.regularisation: Mixup 0.8, Cutmix 1.0, RandAugment (9,0.5), Random Erasing 0.25, label smoothing 0.1, stochastic depth 0.1/0.4/0.5/0.5 (T/S/B/L IN-1K), 0.0/0.0/0.1/0.1/0.2 (IN-22K T/S/B/L/XL), layer scale 1e-6, EMA 0.9999 on IN-1K only
training.seeds: 3 seeds for ResNet-50 regime modernization steps; main results not stated

other.downstream: COCO: Mask R-CNN and Cascade Mask R-CNN, multi-scale training, AdamW, 3x schedule, sweep lr {1e-4,2e-4}, lld {0.7,0.8,0.9,0.95}, stoch depth {0.3..0.8}; ADE20K: UperNet 160K iterations batch 16, sweep lr {8e-5,1e-4}, lld {0.8,0.9}, sd {0.3,0.4,0.5}; MMDetection/MMSegmentation
other.EMA: disabled in the modernization experiments because it hurts BN models
other.resolution: 224^2 default, 384^2 finetune; crop ratio 1.0 at 384^2, 0.875 at 224^2

inference.samples: single run for main tables; 3 seeds in Table 10

other.throughput: V100 per Swin protocol (Table 1); A100 TF32 channels-last PyTorch 1.10 (Table 12)

eval.protocol: Roadmap steps are mean of 3 seeds in ResNet-50 regime; other results are single numbers; Swin COCO/ADE20K numbers from its GitHub repositories.

evidence.quote: There is a 20-epoch linear warmup and a cosine decaying schedule afterward.

results.claim: Modernized ResNet-50 (ConvNeXt-T) reaches higher ImageNet-1K top-1 than Swin-T at similar FLOPs.
results.setup: ResNet-50 regime, 224^2, 300 epochs, ImageNet-1K only, final modernization step
results.quote: We can improve the accuracy to 82.0%, signiﬁcantly exceeding Swin-T’s 81.3%.

results.claim: The improved training recipe alone lifts ResNet-50 from 76.1 to 78.8, so part of the ConvNet-vs-ViT gap is training technique.
results.setup: ResNet-50, 300 epochs, AdamW, Mixup, Cutmix, RandAugment, Random Erasing, Stochastic Depth, Label Smoothing; mean of 3 seeds
results.quote: the performance of the ResNet-50 model from 76.1% [1] to 78.8% (+2.7%)

results.claim: ConvNeXt-XL pre-trained on ImageNet-22K and fine-tuned at 384^2 reaches 87.8% ImageNet-1K top-1.
results.setup: ConvNeXt-XL, 350M params, IN-22K pretrain 90 epochs, finetune 30 epochs, 384^2
results.note: Baseline is Swin-L 384^2 (87.3) and EffNetV2-XL (87.3) from Table 1.
results.quote: our ConvNeXt-XL model achieves an accuracy of 87.8%

results.claim: ConvNeXt-B at 384^2 beats Swin-B by 0.6 points with 12.5% higher V100 throughput (ImageNet-1K only).
results.setup: ImageNet-1K trained then finetuned 384^2, V100 throughput
results.quote: it outperforms Swin-B by 0.6% (85.1% vs. 84.5%), but with 12.5% higher inference throughput (95.7 vs. 85.1 image/s)

results.claim: ConvNeXt-T beats Swin-T on ImageNet-1K by 0.8 points at 224^2.
results.table: Table 1, row ConvNeXt-T 224^2, column IN-1K top-1 acc.

results.claim: On an A100 with TF32 and channels-last, ConvNeXt-S has up to 49% higher throughput than Swin-S.
results.quote: ConvNeXt enjoys up to ∼49% higher throughput compared with a Swin Transformer with similar FLOPs.

results.claim: Largest single gain in the roadmap: removing activations to a single GELU per block adds 0.7 points.
results.quote: This process improves the result by 0.7% to 81.3%, practically matching the performance of Swin-T.

results.claim: Raising the depthwise kernel from 3x3 to 7x7 raises accuracy and saturates at 7x7 at ResNet-50 regime.
results.setup: after moving up depthwise conv (79.9 at 3x3); FLOPs about constant
results.quote: The network’s performance increases from 79.9% (3×3) to 80.6% (7×7)

results.claim: Replacing BN with LN gives a small gain to 81.5 in the modernized model.
ConvNeXt-B (IN-22K, 640^2) beats Swin-B on ADE20K UperNet by 1.4 mIoU multi-scale.
ConvNeXt-XL (IN-22K) reaches 55.2 box AP on COCO with Cascade Mask-RCNN.
results.setup: Cascade Mask-RCNN 3x schedule, multi-scale training, AdamW

results.claim: Isotropic ConvNeXt matches ViT at ImageNet-1K 224^2 (S 79.7 vs 79.8, B 82.0 vs 81.8, L 82.6 vs 82.6).
results.table: Table 2, row ConvNeXt-B (iso.), column IN-1K acc.

results.claim: ConvNeXt-XL IN-22K shows strong robustness on ImageNet-A.
results.setup: ConvNeXt-XL 22K/384^2, no specialised modules or extra finetuning
results.quote: achieving 69.3%/68.2%/55.0% accuracy on ImageNet-A/R/Sketch benchmarks, respectively

results.claim: Training Cascade Mask-RCNN with ConvNeXt-B uses less peak memory than Swin-B.
results.quote: consumes 17.4GB of peak memory with a per-GPU batch size of 2, while the reference number for Swin-B is 18.5GB

results.claim: Inverting dimensions helps more at ResNet-200 than ResNet-50.

limits: Authors concede transformers may be more flexible for multi-modal learning (cross-attention) and tasks needing discretized, sparse or structured outputs (App F).
Roadmap done at small scale first, mostly one seed-averaged ResNet-50 regime; ResNet-200 regime single run.
Compute and hardware for training not stated.
Stage compute ratio likely not optimal (authors).
Throughput advantage measured on V100/A100 of 2021 era; main efficiency claims tied to that hardware.
Swin baselines for COCO/ADE20K taken from public repos, not retrained (except Swin-B/L sweep for COCO).
